arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case argue the significant purpose test protects clients seeking bona fide legal advice.
the opposing sides argue the public has a right to every man's evidence.
the sides that brought the case claim the primary purpose test requires impossible disentangling of purposes.
the opposing sides warn that a significance test creates a sweeping sea change in law.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on the scope of attorney-client privilege. the sides that brought the case argue a significant legal purpose protects mixed communications. the opposing sides argue only a primary legal purpose qualifies for protection.
